# `reset_factory_focal_pos`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Reset the stored focus position to the factory value.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xdbf60, Reset2FactoryFocalPos @0x27db50 (64-bit build) |

Restores the cached factory focal value, writes the camera-specific focal-position configuration if it changed, updates the global focal position and returns it. No focuser movement SDK call is made and the focuser being opened is not checked, so this changes the stored value, not the lens position (INFERRED from the absence of a move call).

Side effects: Updates the global focal position and writes the camera-specific focal_pos configuration if changed (synchronous; the write result is ignored). No motion command. Every full call also makes the shared diagnostic log writes.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"reset_factory_focal_pos"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Optional object only; absent, null, array or scalar params select the local reset. Unknown members are ignored. No positional form. [READ] |
| `params.wide_cam` | boolean\|integer | no | false | Target the wide camera. Boolean or integer (nonzero is true); a wrong type is treated as false. When true: 210 if the wide camera has autofocus; otherwise a process-type-1 device relays the original request to the peer, a process-type-2 device resets locally, and any other process type gives 300. The slave's parser is unresolved. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 210 | wide_cam true and the wide camera has autofocus | `not supported` |
| 300 | wide_cam true under an unsupported process type | `internal error` |
| 236 | Factory focal value is zero or negative | `xml item is not found` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Relay errors are forwarded. A config write failure does not fail the reply.

## Example

Request, default:

```json
{"id":81,"method":"reset_factory_focal_pos"}
```

Request, explicit-local - Shape from the app DTO:

```json
{"id":82,"method":"reset_factory_focal_pos","params":{"wide_cam":false}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"reset_factory_focal_pos","result":{"focal_pos":1500},"code":0,"id":81}
```

Reply, no-factory-value:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"reset_factory_focal_pos","error":"xml item is not found","code":236,"id":83}
```
